title: Tenses
summary: Choose the right English tense for habits, events and results — from the present simple to future forms.

lessons.title: Present Simple
lessons.summary: Habits, routines, permanent facts and timetables.

steps.heading: Present Simple
steps.body: The present simple describes habits, repeated actions and things that are generally true. It is also the tense we use for timetables and fixed schedules, which is why the tense is so common in English even though English has no built-in 'every day' ending. The verb form changes with the subject, and the change matters: adding -s is the difference between a correct sentence and a broken one.

rules.title: Affirmative form
rules.statement: Use the base verb with I, you, we and they, and add -s to the verb with he, she, it and singular nouns.
rules.formula: I / you / we / they + base verb  |  he / she / it + verb-s

examples.en: I drink coffee every morning.
examples.vi: Tôi uống cà phê mỗi sáng.

examples.en: She drinks tea every morning.
examples.vi: Cô ấy uống trà mỗi sáng.

rules.title: Negative and question forms
rules.statement: In the negative and in questions the verb returns to its base form, because the meaning is carried by do or does.
rules.formula: do not / does not + base verb  |  Do / Does + subject + base verb?

examples.en: They don't live here.
examples.vi: Họ không sống ở đây.

examples.en: Does he speak Vietnamese?
examples.vi: Anh ấy có nói tiếng Việt không?

rules.title: Spelling of the -s form
rules.statement: Most verbs add -s. Verbs ending in -o, -ch, -sh, -s and -x add -es, and the irregular forms have, does and go need their own endings.
rules.formula: -o, -ch, -sh, -s, -x + -es  |  have → has, do → does, go → goes

examples.en: He goes to work by bus.
examples.vi: Anh ấy đi làm bằng xe buýt.

examples.en: The shop opens at eight.
examples.vi: Cửa hàng mở cửa lúc tám giờ.

examples.en: My father reads the newspaper every morning.
examples.vi: Bố tôi đọc báo mỗi sáng.
examples.note: habit: every morning signals the present simple

examples.en: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
examples.vi: Nước sôi ở 100 độ C.

examples.en: The train to Hue leaves at 6:45.
examples.vi: Tàu đi Huế khởi hành lúc 6 giờ 45.
examples.note: timetable: the present simple is standard for schedules

examples.en: I don't understand this word.
examples.vi: Tôi không hiểu từ này.

examples.en: Does your sister live near the station?
examples.vi: Chị bạn bạn sống gần nhà ga không?
examples.note: Does + subject + base verb in questions

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: After does not (doesn't), the verb goes back to its base form: like, not likes. The two classic mistakes are both doubles — doesn't don't and doesn't likes — and they show the learner treating -s as part of the present simple instead of the third person ending that does already supplies.

exercises.prompt: He ___ (watch) TV every evening.
exercises.explanation: He is third person singular, so the verb takes -es: watch + -es = watches. Writing watch would be right with I, you, we or they, but with he the ending is obligatory; every evening only tells us it is a habit and does not change the ending.

exercises.prompt: My brother play football on Saturdays.

values: My brother plays football on Saturdays.

exercises.explanation: The subject is my brother, so the third person singular form is needed. A single -s is the whole correction; there is no need for does is playing or any restructuring, because the time marker on Saturdays asks for the simple present in the first place.

exercises.prompt: swim
exercises.instruction: Write the third person singular form of this verb in the present simple.
exercises.explanation: The -s form of swim is regular, so it simply adds -s: he swims. This is worth checking because swim is one of a small set of verbs whose past and past participle are irregular, and learners who over-generalise irregularity sometimes write a doubling form here.

audio.text: My mother goes to the market every Sunday.

acceptedAnswers: My mother goes to the market every Sunday.
items.translation: Mẹ tôi đi chợ mỗi Chủ nhật.

audio.text: The library does not open on public holidays.

acceptedAnswers: The library does not open on public holidays.
items.translation: Thư viện không mở cửa vào những ngày lễ.

questions.prompt: She ___ (teach) English at a primary school.
questions.explanation: Teach ends in -ch, so the third person singular adds -es and keeps the ch: teaches. The -es ending protects the /tʃ/ sound; a bare -s would turn it into /tʃs/, which does not exist in English.

questions.prompt: Write the full form (not the contraction) of the negative present simple of 'do' with 'he'.
questions.explanation: The full form is does not. Learners often answer do not because they choose the form by habit, but do not pairs with I, you, we and they; he and she require does, and the base verb after it stays unchanged.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the present simple correctly?

items.text: The train leave at seven o'clock.
The train leaves at seven o'clock.
The trains is leaving at seven o'clock.
The train is leave at seven o'clock.

questions.explanation: English timetables use the present simple, and the subject the train is singular, so the verb must be leaves. Option c mixes the present simple with the present continuous and also disagrees with the plural trains, and option d puts a base verb after is, which is impossible.

takeaways: The present simple covers habits, repeated actions, general facts and timetables.
Add -s for he, she, it and singular nouns; use -es after -o, -ch, -sh, -s and -x.
In negatives and questions the verb returns to the base form after do, does, don't or doesn't.
Time markers like every day, usually and on Mondays point to the present simple.

lessons.title: Present Continuous
lessons.summary: What is happening now, and what is happening around now.

steps.heading: Present Continuous
steps.body: The present continuous is built with am, is or are plus the -ing form of the verb. It describes an action in progress at the moment of speaking, and also a temporary situation that is true now but will not last. One important job of this tense is contrast: the present simple tells us the habit, the present continuous tells us what is different about today.

rules.title: Form
rules.statement: The tense is always two words: the auxiliary am, is or agree in the present simple, then the verb with -ing.
rules.formula: am / is / are + verb-ing

examples.en: I am studying English now.
examples.vi: Tôi đang học tiếng Anh.

examples.en: They are waiting outside.
examples.vi: Họ đang đứng đợi bên ngoài.

rules.title: Spelling of the -ing form
rules.statement: Normally add -ing to the base verb. Drop a silent e, and double a final consonant after a short stressed vowel when the word is one syllable.
rules.formula: make → making, write → writing, run → running, swim → swimming

examples.en: He is writing a letter.
examples.vi: Anh ấy đang viết thư.

examples.en: The children are running in the yard.
examples.vi: Lũ trẻ đang chạy trong sân.

rules.title: Contrast with the present simple
rules.statement: Use the present simple for the usual routine and the present continuous for what is unusual or temporary this time.
rules.formula: I usually walk. / Today I am walking.

examples.en: She usually cycles to work, but today she is taking the bus.
examples.vi: Bình thường cô ấy đi xe đạp đi làm, nhưng hôm nay cô ấy đang đi xe buýt.

examples.en: The shop usually opens at nine, but today it is opening at ten.
examples.vi: Cửa hàng bình thường mở lúc chín giờ, nhưng hôm nay lại mở lúc mười giờ.
examples.note: present simple = rule, present continuous = today's exception

examples.en: Look! The cat is sleeping on my chair.
examples.vi: Nhìn kìa! Con mèo đang ngủ trên ghế của tôi.
examples.note: an action in progress at the moment of speaking

examples.en: I am reading a very long novel this month.
examples.vi: Tháng này tôi đang đọc một tiểu thuyết rất dài.
examples.note: a temporary situation limited in time

examples.en: We are meeting Mai at the airport tonight.
examples.vi: Tối nay chúng tôi sẽ gặp Mai ở sân bay.
examples.note: a fixed future arrangement often uses the present continuous

examples.en: What are you doing this weekend?
examples.vi: Cuối tuần này bạn đang làm gì?
examples.note: wh- question in the present continuous

examples.en: It is not raining right now.
examples.vi: Ngay lúc này trời đang không mưa.
examples.note: the negative uses not after the auxiliary

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

items.text: She is write an email at the moment.
She is writing an email at the moment.
She is writes an email at the moment.
She writing an email at the moment.

exercises.explanation: After is the verb must be in the -ing form, writing. Option a keeps the base verb, option c adds the present simple -s, and option d leaves out the auxiliary entirely — the present continuous is never made of one word.

exercises.prompt: Listen! Someone ___ (sing) in the next room.
exercises.explanation: The clue is happening right now, so we need the present continuous with is and the -ing form. An English speaker would say is singing, and the is is part of the answer — writing only singing leaves the sentence unfinished.

exercises.prompt: In English, the present continuous is not normally used with verbs of permanent state such as know, believe or love.
exercises.instruction: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
exercises.explanation: The statement is true. Permanent-state verbs resist the progressive: we say I know the answer, not I am knowing the answer. The continuous form only works with actions that have a beginning and an end, which is why verbs like know, believe, own and belong stay in the simple form.

exercises.prompt: My father is watch the news at the moment.

values: My father is watching the news at the moment.

exercises.explanation: The auxiliary is already there, so the verb only needs the -ing ending: watching. Keeping the base form after is is the single most common progressive error in Vietnamese-speaking learners, who translate the English pattern word for word.

audio.text: The students are practising the pronunciation right now.

acceptedAnswers: The students are practising the pronunciation right now.
items.translation: Các học sinh đang luyện phát âm ngay lúc này.

audio.text: She is not working today, so she is coming with us.

acceptedAnswers: She is not working today, so she is coming with us.
items.hint: two present continuous clauses joined by so
items.translation: Hôm nay cô ấy không làm việc, nên cô ấy sẽ đi cùng chúng tôi.

questions.prompt: They ___ (plan) a trip to Sa Pa right now.
questions.explanation: Right now asks for the present continuous, and the subject is they, so the auxiliary is are. The answer needs both parts of the tense: are planning, not just planning.

questions.prompt: I am study for my final exam these days.

values: I am studying for my final exam these days.

questions.explanation: These days is a temporary period around now, so the progressive fits: am studying. Study is a two-syllable word ending in a vowel plus y, so it keeps its spelling and simply takes -ing rather than changing y to i as carry → carried does.

questions.prompt: Bình usually walks to school, but today he ___ a bus because of the rain.
questions.instruction: Pick the option that completes the sentence correctly.
questions.explanation: The pattern usually walks … but today is a classic contrast: habit in the present simple, today's temporary exception in the present continuous. Option d is impossible because a base verb cannot follow is.

takeaways: The present continuous is am, is or are plus the -ing form of the verb.
It describes actions in progress now and temporary situations that will end.
Drop a silent e and double a final consonant after a short stressed vowel: writing, running.
Present simple for the habit, present continuous for today's exception.

lessons.title: Past Simple
lessons.summary: Finished actions at a definite time in the past.

steps.heading: Past Simple
steps.body: The past simple describes an action that started and finished at a known moment in the past. Regular verbs add -ed, and a large group of common verbs is irregular, so the past form has to be learned rather than calculated. Past simple and present continuous are often confused because both talk about a moment in time; the difference is that the past simple is complete and the continuous is unfinished.

rules.title: Form of regular verbs
rules.statement: Add -ed to the base verb. A final silent e is dropped before -ed, and a final consonant after a short stressed vowel is doubled.
rules.formula: work → worked, live → lived, stop → stopped, carry → carried

examples.en: She worked in Hanoi for three years.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đã làm việc ở Hà Nội trong ba năm.
examples.note: regular past, no change to the spelling

examples.en: We travelled to Ninh Binh last summer.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đã đi Ninh Bình vào hè năm ngoái.

rules.title: Irregular verbs
rules.statement: Many frequent verbs change completely in the past, and the same form is used for the past simple and the past participle.
rules.formula: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw, take → took, make → made, write → wrote

examples.en: He went to Da Nang last week.
examples.vi: Anh ấy đã đi Đà Nẵng tuần trước.

examples.en: I ate noodles for lunch.
examples.vi: Tôi đã ăn mì cho bữa trưa.

rules.title: Negatives and questions
rules.statement: The auxiliary did carries the past tense, so the main verb returns to the base form.
rules.formula: did not (didn't) + base verb  |  Did + subject + base verb?

examples.en: I didn't call her yesterday.
examples.vi: Hôm qua tôi đã không gọi cô ấy.

examples.en: Did you finish the report?
examples.vi: Bạn đã xong báo cáo chưa?
examples.note: Did + finish, the -ed is not repeated

rules.title: Time markers
rules.statement: Finished past expressions lock the sentence into the past simple.
rules.formula: yesterday, last night, in 2019, three days ago, when I was a child

examples.en: We met two days ago.
examples.vi: Hai ngày trước chúng tôi đã gặp nhau.
examples.note: two days ago is finished past time

examples.en: I visited my grandparents last Tet.
examples.vi: Tết năm ngoái tôi đã ghé thăm ông bà.
examples.note: finished event with a finished time marker

examples.en: The film started at eight and ended at ten.
examples.vi: Bộ phim bắt đầu lúc tám giờ và kết thúc lúc mười giờ.
examples.note: both ends of the event are given

examples.en: He didn't bring his camera on the trip.
examples.vi: Anh ấy đã không mang máy ảnh khi đi chuyến đi.

examples.en: Did the shop open in 1998?
examples.vi: Cửa hàng đã mở cửa vào năm 1998 chứ?
examples.note: question with Did and a base verb

examples.en: My grandmother told us many stories about the war.
examples.vi: Bà tôi đã kể cho chúng tôi nhiều câu chuyện về cuộc chiến.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

items.text: She didn't went to the party.
She didn't go to the party.
She didn't gone to the party.
She not went to the party.

exercises.explanation: After did not the verb is the base form, go, because did already marks the past. The pair of wrong options a and c shows both forms of the same mistake: keeping the past form went or the past participle gone after the auxiliary.

exercises.prompt: Write the past simple form of the verb 'to buy'.
exercises.explanation: Buy is irregular: buy → bought → bought. It is one of the verbs that has no -ed anywhere, so it has to be memorised as a set of three forms rather than generated by a rule.

exercises.prompt: We ___ (watch) a film about the Mekong Delta last night.
exercises.explanation: Last night is finished past time, so the verb takes the regular -ed ending: watched. Because watch is a two-syllable word ending in a consonant, it does not double the ch.

exercises.prompt: Did you saw the new teacher yesterday?

values: Did you see the new teacher yesterday?

exercises.explanation: The auxiliary Did already carries the past tense, so the main verb must be the base form see. Writing saw doubles the tense, which is the same error pattern as didn't went.

audio.text: We drove to Can Tho during the summer holiday.

acceptedAnswers: We drove to Can Tho during the summer holiday.
items.translation: Chúng tôi đã lái xe đến Cần Thơ trong kỳ nghỉ hè.

audio.text: The match did not start because of the heavy rain.

acceptedAnswers: The match did not start because of the heavy rain.
items.translation: Trận đấu đã không bắt đầu vì mưa lớn.

questions.prompt: I ___ (lose) my keys on the way home yesterday.
questions.explanation: Lose is irregular: lose → lost → lost. Yesterday confirms finished past time, so the irregular past is the only form that fits.

questions.prompt: Which sentence describes a finished action in the past correctly?

items.text: I was watching TV when the phone rang.
I watched TV and then the phone rang.
I have watched TV last night.

questions.explanation: Option b gives two complete past events in order, which is what the past simple is for. Option a is a past action in progress, option c puts a present tense on a finished past time, and option d combines the present perfect with the finished marker last night, which English does not allow.

questions.prompt: They didn't arrived on time for the concert.

values: They didn't arrive on time for the concert.

questions.explanation: Did not is followed by the base verb arrive. Arrived is the regular past form, and the past tense is already in didn't, so the -ed ending is redundant.

takeaways: The past simple describes actions that started and finished at a known past time.
Regular verbs add -ed, with spelling changes such as stopped and carried.
Common frequent verbs are irregular: go → went, buy → bought, see → saw.
In negatives and questions, did carries the tense and the verb returns to its base form.

lessons.title: Present Perfect
lessons.summary: Past events linked to now: experience, results, unfinished time.

steps.heading: Present Perfect
steps.body: The present perfect links a past event to the present moment: either the result is still true now, or the event is simply part of our experience. Because the present perfect points at now rather than at a finished time, it cannot be used with yesterday, last week or in 2019. The form is have or has plus the past participle, which is the same form you use after a modal in a perfect construction.

rules.title: Form
rules.statement: Use have or has with the past participle of the main verb. The participle of a regular verb is the -ed form; for an irregular verb it is the third form in the list.
rules.formula: have / has + past participle

examples.en: I have finished my homework.
examples.vi: Tôi đã làm xong bài tập.
examples.note: have + finished; the result is true now

examples.en: She has gone to Hue.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đã đi Huế rồi.

rules.title: Present perfect or past simple?
rules.statement: Use the past simple with a finished time, and the present perfect when the time is open or the connection to now is the point.
rules.formula: I saw him yesterday. / I have seen him three times.

examples.en: We visited the old citadel in 2018.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đã tham quan thành cổ vào năm 2018.
examples.note: in 2018 is finished, so past simple

examples.en: I have visited the old citadel twice.
examples.vi: Tôi đã tham quan thành cổ hai lần.
examples.note: twice is not a finished time, so present perfect

rules.title: For and since
rules.statement: For measures a length of time, since names the starting point. Both describe a situation that started in the past and is still true.
rules.formula: for + period (three years, a long time) | since + point (2019, Monday, I was a student)

examples.en: She has lived in Hanoi for five years.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đã sống ở Hà Nội được năm năm.

examples.en: He has worked here since 2019.
examples.vi: Anh ấy đã làm việc ở đây từ năm 2019.

rules.title: Negatives and questions
rules.statement: The auxiliary have or has behaves like any other auxiliary: never has it in negatives and questions, and the participle never changes.
rules.formula: have not (haven't) + participle | Have / Has + subject + participle?

examples.en: I haven't seen him since we graduated.
examples.vi: Tôi chưa gặp anh ấy kể từ khi chúng tôi tốt nghiệp.

examples.en: Has the package arrived yet?
examples.vi: Gói hàng đã đến chưa?

examples.en: I have never been to Japan.
examples.vi: Tôi chưa bao giờ đến Nhật Bản.

examples.en: She has just left the office.
examples.vi: Cô ấy vừa rời khỏi văn phòng.
examples.note: just places the event very near now

examples.en: We have known each other for ten years.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đã quen nhau mười năm.
examples.note: situation that is still true now

examples.en: Have you finished the report yet?
examples.vi: Bạn đã xong báo cáo chưa?
examples.note: yet in a question about an unfinished situation

examples.en: He has written three emails so far.
examples.vi: Anh ấy đã viết ba email cho đến giờ.
examples.note: so far keeps the time open

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Yesterday is a finished time, so English requires the past simple saw. The present perfect cannot take a finished time marker because it deliberately leaves the time open; the other options also confuse the participle seen with the past form saw.

exercises.prompt: Which time expressions can go with the present perfect? Select all that apply.
exercises.explanation: So far, since 2020 and never all leave the time open or point at a starting point, which is exactly what the present perfect needs. Last Tuesday and two days ago are finished points in time, so they force the past simple instead.

exercises.prompt: They ___ (not eat) anything since they arrived.
exercises.explanation: Since they arrived is a starting point, so the sentence needs has or have plus the participle eaten. The past participle of eat is eaten, not ate; that form belongs to the past simple.

exercises.prompt: I have bought this bike last year.

values: I bought this bike last year.

exercises.explanation: Last year is a finished time, so the present perfect is not available and the past simple bought is the right choice. The other possible repair, I have owned this bike since last year, would be correct too, but the minimal fix keeps last year and changes the tense.

audio.text: I have already sent the invitation to her.

acceptedAnswers: I have already sent the invitation to her.
items.translation: Tôi đã gửi lời mời cho cô ấy rồi.

audio.text: They have not finished building the new library yet.

acceptedAnswers: They have not finished building the new library yet.
items.translation: Họ chưa xong việc xây thư viện mới.

questions.prompt: Write the past participle of the verb 'to write'.
questions.explanation: Write is irregular: write → wrote → written. The third form, written, is what you need after have, has, should and other modals; mixing up wrote and written is the single most common irregular-verb error in this tense.

questions.prompt: She has went to the countryside three times.

values: She has gone to the countryside three times.

questions.explanation: After has we need the past participle, and the participle of go is gone. Went is the past simple form, which is only correct with a finished time, and three times is not one.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly contrasts the two tenses?

items.text: I have met her in 2019 and I still remember her face.
I met her in 2019 and I still remember her face.
I have met her since 2019 and I still remember her face.
I met her for 2019 and I still remember her face.

questions.explanation: In 2019 is a finished point in time, so the first clause must be the past simple met; the second clause is in the present simple, which is the normal pattern for expressing a result that still holds. Option c would work with since 2019, but not with in 2019, and option d mixes for with a date.

takeaways: The present perfect links a past event to now: experience, results or an unfinished situation.
It is have or has plus the past participle, the same participle used after modals.
It never takes a finished time marker such as yesterday or in 2019.
For measures a length of time; since names a starting point.

lessons.title: Past Continuous
lessons.summary: What was in progress at a past moment, and interrupted actions.

steps.heading: Past Continuous
steps.body: The past continuous is was or were plus the -ing form, and it looks back at a past moment to describe an unfinished background action. Its main job is to set the scene for a shorter event: the long action was in progress, and then something short interrupted it. The long action is normally expressed with the past continuous and the short action with the past simple.

rules.title: Form
rules.statement: Use the past form of be with the -ing form of the verb, with the same spelling rules as the present continuous.
rules.formula: was / were + verb-ing

examples.en: I was cooking dinner at eight o'clock.
examples.vi: Lúc tám giờ tôi đang nấu bữa tối.
examples.note: was + cooking, an unfinished past action

examples.en: They were waiting for the bus.
examples.vi: Họ đang đợi xe buýt.

rules.title: Long action, short interruption
rules.statement: The action in progress takes the past continuous; the interrupting, shorter event takes the past simple.
rules.formula: I was reading when the lights went out.

examples.en: She was typing an email when her boss came in.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đang gõ email thì sếp bước vào.

examples.en: We were walking home and it started to rain.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đang đi bộ về nhà thì trời bắt đầu mưa.
examples.note: started is the new, short event

rules.title: While and when
rules.statement: While introduces the longer action in progress; when introduces the shorter interrupting event. The two words are often interchangeable, but the meaning shifts slightly.
rules.formula: while + past continuous, when + past simple

examples.en: While I was cooking, my brother called.
examples.vi: Trong lúc tôi đang nấu ăn, anh trai tôi gọi điện.

examples.en: I dropped a plate when the dog ran into the kitchen.
examples.vi: Tôi làm rơi một cái đĩa khi con chó chạy vào bếp.

rules.title: Two actions in progress together
rules.statement: When two past actions overlap and neither interrupts the other, both can take the past continuous, and while is the natural linker.
rules.formula: I was cooking while she was setting the table.

examples.en: While I was cooking, she was setting the table.
examples.vi: Trong lúc tôi nấu ăn thì cô ấy đang bày bàn.

examples.en: The sky was getting darker and the wind was rising.
examples.vi: Bầu trời đang tối dần và gió đang mạnh lên.
examples.note: two backgrounds in progress in the past

examples.en: I wasn't listening when she asked the question.
examples.vi: Tôi đã không lắng nghe khi cô ấy đặt câu hỏi.
examples.note: wasn't + listening is a background action

examples.en: What were you doing at ten last night?
examples.vi: Lúc mười giờ đêm qua bạn đang làm gì?
examples.note: question in the past continuous about an interrupted activity

examples.en: They were playing badminton when the rain stopped.
examples.vi: Họ đang chơi cầu lông thì mưa ngừng.
examples.note: playing continues, stopped marks the new event

examples.en: While she was waiting, a stranger offered her a seat.
examples.vi: Trong lúc cô ấy đứng đợi, một người lạ đã nhường ghế cho cô ấy.

exercises.prompt: While I ___, the phone rang.
exercises.instruction: Pick the option that completes the sentence correctly.
exercises.explanation: While introduces the longer action in progress, so it needs the past continuous: was cooking. The other options describe a completed action, a present situation, or a link to now, none of which set the background for a past interruption.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanation: The subject comes first, then was and the -ing form, then the when clause with the short past simple event. The order was she was reading when the lights went out teaches the whole long-action / short-interruption pattern in one sentence.

exercises.prompt: They ___ (not watch) TV when I entered the room.
exercises.explanation: The subject is they, so the auxiliary is were, and the action is in progress, so the participle is watching. Watched would describe a finished action and would remove the background meaning the sentence needs.

exercises.prompt: I was study when the bell rang.

values: I was studying when the bell rang.

exercises.explanation: The auxiliary was requires the -ing form, so the verb becomes studying. Just as is never takes a base verb, was never takes one either; this is the same progressive error as in the present continuous, only in the past.

audio.text: While she was revising for her exam, her brother was making noise.

acceptedAnswers: While she was revising for her exam, her brother was making noise.
items.translation: Trong lúc cô ấy đang ôn thi, anh trai cô ấy đang gây ồn.

audio.text: We were having dinner when the power went out.

acceptedAnswers: We were having dinner when the power went out.
items.translation: Chúng tôi đang ăn tối thì mất điện.

items.text: He was sleep when I called him.
He was sleeping when I called him.
He was slept when I called him.
He is sleeping when I called him.

questions.explanation: Was needs the -ing form, so the verb is sleeping, and the interruption is in the past simple: called. Option c uses the past participle after a progressive auxiliary, and option d mixes a present tense with a past clause.

questions.prompt: Write the full form (not the contraction) of the negative past continuous of 'to be' with 'she'.
questions.explanation: With she the past auxiliary is was, so the full negative is was not. Learners often write did not because the sentence is about the past, but the past continuous does not use did at all — that is a feature of the past simple only.

questions.prompt: Complete with the past continuous: 'They ___ dinner when the doorbell rang.'
questions.explanation: The background action takes the past continuous, so the phrase is were having. Having is the -ing form of have, and with a plural subject the auxiliary is were, not was.

takeaways: The past continuous is was or were plus the -ing form of the verb.
It describes an unfinished action at a past moment, usually as background.
The long interrupted action takes the past continuous; the short interrupter takes the past simple.
While normally introduces the background, when the interruption.

lessons.title: Future Forms
lessons.summary: will, going to, the present continuous for the future, and the future perfect.

steps.heading: Future Forms
steps.body: English has no single way to talk about the future, and the choice carries meaning. Will expresses a decision made now, a promise, an offer or a prediction based on opinion; going to expresses an intention formed earlier or a prediction based on present evidence. Two present forms also cover the future: the present continuous for fixed arrangements and the present simple for timetables. The future perfect completes the system by looking back from a future point.

rules.title: Will and going to
rules.statement: Will is for spontaneous decisions, promises, offers and opinion-based predictions. Going to is for intentions decided before now and for predictions based on visible evidence.
rules.formula: will + base verb | be going to + base verb

examples.en: I'll help you with those bags.
examples.vi: Tôi sẽ giúp bạn mang những túi đó.
examples.note: an offer decided at the moment of speaking

examples.en: Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.
examples.vi: Nhìn những đám mây kia, trời sắp mưa rồi.
examples.note: prediction from evidence we can see now

rules.title: Present forms for the future
rules.statement: The present continuous is used for arrangements agreed in advance, and the present simple for timetables and programmes.
rules.formula: am / is / are + verb-ing | present simple for schedules

examples.en: I'm meeting the dentist on Friday.
examples.vi: Tôi sẽ gặp bác sĩ răng vào thứ Sáu.

examples.en: The plane departs at 6:15 tomorrow.
examples.vi: Máy bay cất cánh lúc 6 giờ 15 ngày mai.

rules.title: The future perfect
rules.statement: Will have plus the past participle looks back from a future point to an action that will be finished by then. Time phrases such as by then, by the time and before usually accompany it.
rules.formula: will have + past participle

examples.en: By next June I will have graduated.
examples.vi: Đến tháng Sáu tới tôi sẽ đã tốt nghiệp.

examples.en: She will have finished the report by noon tomorrow.
examples.vi: Đến trưa mai cô ấy sẽ đã xong báo cáo.

rules.title: Time clauses with will
rules.statement: In a when, if, as soon as or before clause about the future, English normally uses the present simple or present continuous, not will.
rules.formula: I'll call you as soon as I arrive.

examples.en: I'll call you as soon as I arrive at the airport.
examples.vi: Tôi sẽ gọi cho bạn ngay khi tôi đến sân bay.

examples.en: She won't leave until the meeting finishes.
examples.vi: Cô ấy sẽ không đi cho đến khi cuộc họp kết thúc.

examples.en: I think you will do well in the interview.
examples.vi: Tôi nghĩ bạn sẽ làm tốt trong cuộc phỏng vấn.

examples.en: We're going to visit our grandparents this weekend.
examples.vi: Cuối tuần này chúng tôi dự định đi thăm ông bà.

examples.en: The bus leaves from bay four at half past six.
examples.vi: Xe buýt xuất phát từ số 4 lúc sáu giờ rưỡi.

examples.en: By the time you get here, we will have finished.
examples.vi: Đến lúc bạn tới nơi thì chúng tôi sẽ đã xong rồi.
examples.note: future perfect with by the time

examples.en: I'll let you know as soon as I hear from her.
examples.vi: Tôi sẽ báo bạn ngay khi nào nhận được tin cô ấy.
examples.note: will in the main clause, present simple after as soon as

exercises.prompt: The bag is very heavy. — 'I ___ you with it.'
exercises.explanation: The offer is made at the moment of speaking, which is the job of will. Going to would suggest the speaker had already decided to help, and the bare base verb has no future marking at all.

exercises.prompt: Which sentences are correct English? Select all that apply.

items.text: I'll text you when I will arrive.
I'll text you when I arrive.
By December she will have been here for ten years.
By December she will be here since ten years.

exercises.explanation: A future time clause takes a present form, so when I arrive is right and when I will arrive is not. Option c is a correct future perfect with a by phrase; option d mixes by with since, and since does not belong after by.

exercises.prompt: By the time we get to the station, the train will left.

values: By the time we get to the station, the train will have left.

exercises.explanation: The action will be finished before the future point named in the first clause, so we need the future perfect: will have left. Left is the past participle on its own, which needs the auxiliary have; will left is not possible in English.

exercises.prompt: Translate into English: 'Đến cuối năm nay tôi sẽ đã sống ở đây được ba năm.'
exercises.translation: By the end of this year I will have lived here for three years.

values: By the end of this year I will have lived here for three years.

exercises.explanation: The Vietnamese đến cuối năm nay marks a deadline in the future, so English needs by the end of this year plus the future perfect will have lived. A simple future will live would lose the idea that the three years will already be complete by then.

exercises.prompt: Look at that child — he ___ (spill) the whole glass.
exercises.explanation: There is visible evidence right now, so English predicts with going to. Will would express an opinion or a decision, and the present continuous would suggest an arrangement already agreed rather than a prediction.

audio.text: I will let you know as soon as the results come out.

acceptedAnswers: I will let you know as soon as the results come out.
items.hint: will in the main clause, present simple after as soon as
items.translation: Tôi sẽ báo bạn ngay khi có kết quả.

audio.text: By the end of the course we will have learned two thousand words.

acceptedAnswers: By the end of the course we will have learned two thousand words.
items.hint: by the end of + future perfect
items.translation: Đến cuối khóa học chúng ta sẽ đã học được hai nghìn từ.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a future form in both parts?

items.text: I will call you as soon as I will get home.
I will call you as soon as I get home.
I will call you as soon as I got home.
I am going to call you as soon as I will get home.

questions.explanation: English does not put will in a future time clause, so as soon as I get home is the natural form. Option c uses the past simple, which would suggest a routine in the past rather than a single future event.

questions.prompt: By next March I will finish my degree.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence so that it expresses a completed result before March.

values: By next March I will have finished my degree.

questions.explanation: A by phrase pointing to a future deadline normally pairs with the future perfect when the focus is on completion: will have finished. The simple future is also possible, but it treats the finishing as the event rather than a state already achieved by that date.

questions.prompt: Write the past participle of the verb 'to be'.
questions.explanation: Be → was or were → been. Been is the participle used in have been and will have been; learners often write was, which is a past form and cannot follow have or will have.

takeaways: Will covers decisions made now, promises, offers and opinion-based predictions.
Going to covers intentions formed earlier and predictions based on present evidence.
The present continuous covers fixed arrangements; the present simple covers timetables.
Will have plus the past participle looks back from a future point, usually with by.
Future time clauses take a present form: as soon as I arrive, not as soon as I will arrive.
